proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 7.2 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 2020–2135), "only if" part. It uses the Deformation Theorem 5.3 (lines 1461–1480), the completeness Lemma 3.13 (lines 901–935) and the slicing Lemma 4.5 (here the sibling slicing).
Correction: Simon's localization step ("we can assume without loss of generality that W ⊂⊂ U and spt T_j ⊆ W̄") also needs the localized currents to converge weakly to the localized limit. Step 1 chooses the cutting level so that this holds.
Notation: for integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and open Ŵ ⊆ U, d_Ŵ(A, B) := inf{M_Ŵ(R) + M_Ŵ(S) : A − B = ∂R + S in U, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity} (Simon 7.1). μ_A is the measure of a representation of A, and M_V(A) = μ_A(V) for open V by (C1). For Borel E, A⌞E is the current of sibling borel_restriction. Integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (sibling int_combination). If n > P every n-current is 0 and the claim is trivial (R_j = 0, S_j = 0), so assume n ≤ P.
0. Reduction.
 (a) Fix W open with W̄ a compact subset of U. If W = ∅ then M_W ≡ 0, and R_j := 0, S_j := T − T_j (integer multiplicity by int_combination) work; so assume W ≠ ∅. For each j, d_W(T, T_j) ≤ M_W(T − T_j) < ∞, taking R = 0 and S = T − T_j.
 (b) It suffices to show (★): every subsequence of (T_j) has a further subsequence (T_{j_ℓ}) with d_W(T, T_{j_ℓ}) → 0. Indeed, (★) gives a_j := d_W(T, T_j) → 0. Choosing for each j integer multiplicity R_j, S_j with T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) ≤ a_j + 2^{−j} then proves the theorem.
 (c) Every subsequence satisfies all hypotheses. So it is enough to find one subsequence of (T_j) along which d_W(T, ·) → 0.
1. Localization (Simon: "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2").
 Let f(x) := dist(x, W̄), a 1-Lipschitz function (W̄ is compact and nonempty). Choose δ > 0 with {f ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U, e.g. δ := dist(W̄, ℝ^P ∖ U)/4 (δ := 1 if U = ℝ^P); {f ≤ 3δ} is closed and bounded, hence compact. Put W'' := {f < 3δ} and Λ := sup_j M_{W''}(T_j) < ∞.
 (a) Monotone functions. The functions g_j(s) := μ_{T_j}({f < s}), s ∈ [δ, 3δ], are nondecreasing and bounded by Λ. By Helly's selection theorem a subsequence (not relabelled) has g_j → g pointwise on [δ, 3δ], with g nondecreasing. g is continuous outside a countable set.
 (b) Slices. Write n = (n − 1) + 1 and apply slicing to T_j, with RB the empty triple representing ∂T_j = 0, the function f and L = 1. This gives P_{j,s} ∈ 𝒟_{n−1}(U) with ∫ M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ M_{W''}(T_j) ≤ Λ. For a.e. s, P_{j,s} is integer multiplicity and P_{j,s}(ω) = ∫_{M_j∩{f<s}} θ_j ξ_j(dω) dHⁿ for all ω, where (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) represents T_j. Fatou's lemma (for a.e.-measurable integrands) gives ∫_δ^{2δ} liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,s}) ds ≤ Λ.
 (c) Choice of level. Choose t ∈ (δ, 2δ) such that g is continuous at t, (b) holds at s = t for every j, and liminf_j M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) < ∞; each condition excludes only a null set. Pass to a further subsequence with Λ' := sup_j M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) < ∞. Put W₁ := {f < t}, which is open with W̄ ⊆ W₁, and K₁ := {f ≤ t}, which is compact with W̄₁ ⊆ K₁ ⊆ W''.
 (d) Localized currents. Put T̂_j := T_j⌞W₁ and T̂ := T⌞W₁; they are integer multiplicity by borel_restriction.
 (i) ∂T̂_j(ω) = T̂_j(dω) = ∫_{M_j∩W₁} θ_j ξ_j(dω) = P_{j,t}(ω). So ∂T̂_j = P_{j,t} is integer multiplicity, and M(∂T̂_j) = M_{W''}(P_{j,t}) ≤ Λ' by (C1), because P_{j,t} vanishes off f⁻¹(t) ⊆ W''.
 (ii) M(T̂_j) = μ_{T_j}(W₁) ≤ Λ.
 (iii) T̂_j and T̂ vanish on forms supported in U ∖ K₁.
 (iv) T̂_j ⇀ T̂. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and let s > 0 be small. Take smooth φ_s : ℝ^P → [0,1] with φ_s = 1 on {f ≤ t − s} and spt φ_s ⊆ {f < t}. Then 1_{W₁} − φ_s is supported in {t − s < f < t} ⊆ {f < t} ∖ {f < t − s}, and |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for unit simple ξ. Hence |T̂_j(ω) − T_j(φ_sω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ (g_j(t) − g_j(t − s)) and |T̂(ω) − T(φ_sω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ μ_T({t − s < f < t}). Since T_j(φ_sω) → T(φ_sω),
 limsup_j |T̂_j(ω) − T̂(ω)| ≤ sup‖ω‖ (g(t) − g(t − s) + μ_T({t − s < f < t})).
 The right side tends to 0 as s ↓ 0, by continuity of g at t and because the sets {t − s < f < t} decrease to ∅ and have finite μ_T-measure.
2. Total boundedness (Simon (1)–(3)).
 Let K₂ := {f ≤ 5δ/2} (compact ⊆ U) and M₀ := Λ + Λ'.
 Claim: for every ε > 0 there are finitely many integer multiplicity Π₁, …, Π_N ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with the following property. Let A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, vanishing on forms supported in U ∖ K₁, with ∂A integer multiplicity and M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀. Then A − Π_i = ∂R + S' for some i and some integer multiplicity R, S' vanishing on forms supported in U ∖ K₂, with M(R) + M(S') < ε.
 Proof of the claim:
 (a) Regard A as a current in ℝ^P (extension by zero; spt A ⊆ K₁).
 (b) If n < P, apply the Deformation Theorem 5.3 with grid size λ. It gives A − Π = ∂R + S' with Π = Σ_{F∈F_n(λ)} β_F[[F]], β_F ∈ ℤ. The estimates are M(Π) ≤ cM(A), M(R) ≤ cλM(A) and M(S') ≤ cλM(∂A), with c = c(n, P). The supports satisfy spt Π ∪ spt R ∪ spt S' ⊆ {dist(·, K₁) < 2√P λ}. Π, R and S' are integer multiplicity because A and ∂A are.
 (c) If n = P, embed ℝ^P = ℝ^P × {0} ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} by the linear isometry i. Then i_#A = τ(i(M_A), θ_A∘i⁻¹, (∧_P i)ξ_A) and ∂(i_#A) = i_#∂A are integer multiplicity, with the same masses as A and ∂A. Apply 5.3 to i_#A in ℝ^{P+1} (codimension 1), with support radius 2√(P+1)·λ. Push the result back with the orthogonal projection p : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ^P; this is defined on the compactly supported currents involved (Ch. 6, 2.23). p is linear with ‖p‖ = 1 and p∘i = id, so p_# does not increase mass and p_#i_#A = A. Since p_#R is a (P+1)-current in ℝ^P, it is 0. Hence A − p_#Π = p_#S'.
  - p_#Π = Σ_F β_F p_#[[F]]. If the P-face F is parallel to ℝ^P × {0}, p maps F isometrically onto a grid cube of ℝ^P and p_#[[F]] = ±[[p(F)]]. Otherwise F contains the e_{P+1} direction, Dp maps its tangent plane onto a (P−1)-dimensional space, ∧_P Dp vanishes on it, and p_#[[F]] = 0. So p_#Π is an integer combination of grid cubes, integer multiplicity by int_combination, with M(p_#Π) ≤ M(Π) ≤ cM(A).
  - S'' := A − p_#Π = p_#S' is integer multiplicity by int_combination, and M(S'') ≤ M(S') ≤ cλM(∂A).
  In the claim, use p_#Π in place of Π, R := 0, and S'' in place of S'. No appeal to Simon 3.9 (Lipschitz push-forward) is needed here.
 (d) Choose λ with 2√(P+1)·λ < δ/2 and 2cλM₀ < ε. Then in both cases the supports lie in K₂ and M(R) + M(S') < ε; restricted to U, the identity A − Π = ∂R + S' (with p_#Π, S'' when n = P) holds in U.
 (e) Finiteness. The cells F ∈ F_n(λ) meeting {dist(·, K₁) < δ/2} (in ℝ^P, or in ℝ^{P+1} when n = P) are finitely many, and |β_F|λⁿ ≤ M(Π) ≤ cM₀. So only finitely many Π, and hence finitely many p_#Π, occur.
3. Cauchy subsequence.
 (a) By 1(d), the currents T̂_j satisfy the hypotheses of step 2.
 (b) Apply step 2 with ε = 2^{−r−1} for r = 1, 2, …. By pigeonhole, choose infinite index sets J₁ ⊇ J₂ ⊇ ⋯ and integer multiplicity Π_r such that, for all j ∈ J_r, T̂_j − Π_r = ∂R + S' with R, S' integer multiplicity, vanishing off K₂ and M(R) + M(S') < 2^{−r−1}. Pick j_r ∈ J_r with j₁ < j₂ < ⋯.
 (c) Since j_r and j_{r+1} both lie in J_r, subtracting the two decompositions gives T̂_{j_{r+1}} − T̂_{j_r} = ∂R_r + S_r. Here R_r, S_r are integer multiplicity (int_combination), vanish off K₂, and satisfy M(R_r) + M(S_r) < 2^{−r}.
4. Summation (Simon (5) and Lemma 3.13).
 (a) Fix ℓ. The partial sums Σ_{r=ℓ}^m R_r and Σ_{r=ℓ}^m S_r are integer multiplicity (int_combination), vanish off K₂, and are Cauchy for the mass M.
 (b) By the completeness Lemma 3.13 they converge in mass to integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} with M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
 (c) Mass convergence implies weak convergence, and ∂ is weakly continuous. So for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), T̂_{j_m}(ω) − T̂_{j_ℓ}(ω) = Σ_{r=ℓ}^{m−1}(∂R_r + S_r)(ω) → (∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)})(ω) as m → ∞.
 (d) By 1(d)(iv) the left side of (c) also tends to T̂(ω) − T̂_{j_ℓ}(ω). Hence T̂ − T̂_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)}.
5. Back to T and T_j.
 (a) T − T̂ = T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ W₁) and T_{j_ℓ} − T̂_{j_ℓ} = T_{j_ℓ}⌞(ℝ^P ∖ W₁), by additivity of the defining integrals. These are integer multiplicity (borel_restriction) and vanish on forms supported in W₁ ⊇ W.
 (b) Put S̃_ℓ := S^{(ℓ)} + (T − T̂) − (T_{j_ℓ} − T̂_{j_ℓ}), which is integer multiplicity by int_combination. By 4(d), T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S̃_ℓ.
 (c) By subadditivity of M_W and vanishing on W, M_W(R^{(ℓ)}) + M_W(S̃_ℓ) ≤ M(R^{(ℓ)}) + M(S^{(ℓ)}) ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
 So d_W(T, T_{j_ℓ}) → 0 along the subsequence chosen in steps 1–3, which by step 0 proves the theorem. ∎
key_steps: Reduce to: every subsequence has a further subsequence with d_W(T, T_j) → 0; then pick near-optimal decompositions.
Localize to W₁ = {dist(·, W̄) < t}: slicing plus Fatou bound M(∂(T_j⌞W₁)); a Helly-continuity level t makes T_j⌞W₁ ⇀ T⌞W₁.
Deformation Theorem: integer multiplicity cycles with bounded mass and boundary mass on a fixed compact are totally bounded in flat distance.
A Cauchy subsequence and completeness (Lemma 3.13) give T⌞W₁ − T_{j_ℓ}⌞W₁ = ∂R^{(ℓ)} + S^{(ℓ)} with masses ≤ 2^{1−ℓ}.
Add back the parts outside W₁, which carry no mass in W, to get T − T_{j_ℓ} = ∂R + S̃ with small M_W.
